Holiday standards for kennel doors for new staff
This page shows new staff a habit of care

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps kennel doors in good order because small lapses can unsettle an animal and delay a clean handoff. When you prepare a kennel, check the latch, the hinges, the frame, and the visible seal before the pet is moved. If the door swings unevenly or does not sit flush, stop and report it at once. Keep your tone calm around travelers and speak in plain language so owners know their pet is being handled with care.

The desk ledger must reflect every service change that affects the pet cabin or the kennel assignment. Record the issue clearly, add the action taken, and pass the note to the next shift without delay. This is routine work, but it matters because the cabin team relies on accurate entries to monitor animals during flight. If a traveler such as Arjun Sato or Zain Andersson asks about a kennel change, answer briefly and direct the matter through the normal desk process. Do not guess, and do not promise a fix until the kennel has been checked.

When a pet is due for boarding, keep the door closed until the carrier is seated and the handler confirms the fit. If you see Miso, or any other pet, showing stress at the counter, lower your voice and slow your movements. New staff should remember that door control is not a side task. It is part of safe handling, and it helps preserve trust with each traveler who comes to Aurelia Skyways for support.

Finish every check with a final look at the latch and a clean note in the ledger. What to remember is simple: secure the door, write the change, and keep the handoff steady.
